finding: Official batch recovery records produced by tasks import and batch skip can be rejected by the pre-commit cross-task mutation guard as ordinary cross-task edits, forcing a governed operator to use an emergency hook bypass even when every staged file is the exact audit trail for dependency-blocked queue-head triage.
expectedBehavior: Pre-commit should recognize and validate official batch skip/import audit bundles as a first-class governed mutation class, with exact task/event/file constraints, so dependency-blocked batch triage can be committed without raw hook bypass.
evidenceOrRepro: The focused regression tests the former cross-task refusal path with a real staged atm.taskTransition.v1 batch-skip event. It admits only when the event actor is the active committing claim actor and the runtime batch record has the same batchId and contains both the committing task and the skipped task; a mismatched batch identity remains blocked. This closes the official batch recovery route without a broad cross-task exemption.
followUp: Keep batch recovery events bound to the runtime batch record and active claim actor; any future batch audit action must add an equally narrow regression before admission is widened.
